member.name: T:Durable.CosmosDb.CosmosDbBackend
member.summary:
An Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL : stores entities as JSON documents in a Cosmos DB database. Use it through (or any ); one backend wraps one and database and serves every entity type, so includes and navigation predicates work across repositories that share it. Create one backend per database and share it.
Storage: each entity type is a container named (created on first use), each mapped column a document property named after the column, written by Durable from with System.Text.Json through the SDK's stream APIs (the SDK's reflection serializer is never used for entities). The document id is the primary key as text (composite keys joined with |); a single primary key column named id with string values is the id itself, and a column named id that is not is stored as durable_id. Values are stored the way a database driver would ( provider values, JSON text for JSON columns, enum names or numbers) and encoded losslessly and so that Cosmos DB orders them like C# (see for partition keys): numbers as JSON numbers, DateTime as fixed-width ISO 8601 wall-clock text plus a kind suffix (Z, none, or the local offset), DateTimeOffset as its UTC instant (...Z), DateOnly as yyyy-MM-dd, TimeSpan and TimeOnly as ticks, Guid as lowercase text, byte arrays as base64. Because Cosmos DB may hold JSON numbers only as doubles, longs beyond plus or minus 2^53 and decimals a double cannot round-trip keep an exact copy under the document's _durable object, as does the offset of a DateTimeOffset; reads use it. Decimal scale (trailing zeros) is not preserved. Auto-increment values come from a counter document per container (see ) incremented with an ETag-conditioned replace, so concurrent creates never share a key, also across processes. Inserting a duplicate primary key throws . Cosmos DB indexes every property; needs no action, and is not enforced (Cosmos DB unique keys apply only within a logical partition and only at container creation).
Queries: the parts of a filter whose Cosmos DB semantics match C# (see ) are pushed down as a parameterized Cosmos DB SQL query, with a single-key ORDER BY, OFFSET/LIMIT, COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX when the whole query is exact; key lookups are point reads. Everything else (functions, navigations, multi-key ordering, grouping, residual filters) is evaluated client-side with C# semantics over the documents Cosmos DB returns, so push-down never changes results. Strings compare ordinally and case-sensitively, so behaves as . Unordered queries return documents in primary key order.
Writes: every single-document write is atomic. Updates and deletes read the matching documents and write each one with an ETag condition (If-Match); when another writer changed a document first, it is read again, re-checked against the condition (for example the expected version) and written again, so optimistic concurrency and set-based updates never lose updates. A write that matches several documents is not atomic as a whole, and neither is a change of a document's id or partition key (create the new document, then delete the old one). Transactions are not supported ( is absent): Cosmos DB transactional batches cover only one logical partition, so Durable does not pretend to offer atomicity across documents.
Lifetime: create a backend with (or ), share it across repositories, and dispose it when done. It disposes the client only when it created it (); a client passed in with is never disposed. Repositories never dispose the backend.
Trimming and Native AOT: not supported. The Azure Cosmos DB SDK (Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos) uses Newtonsoft.Json and reflection internally, so and carry [RequiresUnreferencedCode] and [RequiresDynamicCode]. Durable's own code in this package is trim-annotated and warning-free.
Thread safety: safe for concurrent use by any number of repositories and threads.

member.name: T:Durable.CosmosDb.CosmosDbPushdown
member.summary:
Translates the parts of a filter whose Cosmos DB semantics match C# into a parameterized Cosmos DB SQL condition. The filter is split into AND-ed conjuncts; each conjunct is translated when it is built from comparisons, null checks, Contains (IN) lists, string matches (StartsWith, EndsWith, Contains) and IsNullOrEmpty on a column of the queried source against client-side values, combined with AND, OR and NOT; anything else (functions, arithmetic, navigations, columns compared with columns) is left to client-side evaluation. Every translated condition is total (true or false, never undefined, guarded by IS_NUMBER / IS_STRING / IS_BOOL, with C# null semantics through IS_DEFINED / IS_NULL) and a necessary condition of the filter, so evaluating the full filter client-side afterwards never changes results; when every conjunct translated exactly, is true and Cosmos DB's result is final.
Exactness rules: parameters are converted to the column's stored form and must have its stored type (integers may mix widths). Integers, booleans, Guids, dates, DateTimeOffset instants, floats and doubles compare exactly (NaN and infinities, stored as strings, are included explicitly where C# orders them). Strings compare exactly for equality, string matches and IN; ordering comparisons are exact when the parameter has no character at or above U+D800 (where Cosmos DB's code point order differs from UTF-16 ordinal order). DateTime compares by its fixed-width wall-clock prefix (ticks, ignoring the kind, like C#). Long values beyond plus or minus 2^53 and decimals that a double cannot round-trip may be compared as doubles inside Cosmos DB: comparisons with such a parameter are widened (non-strict) and re-checked client-side; comparisons of a decimal column with an exact parameter are exact unless the column holds such decimals, which lets the backend probe for (translate again with conservativeDecimals when it does). Case-insensitive matches are pushed with Cosmos DB's case-insensitive functions only for ASCII patterns without i, I, s or S (whose case folding differs from ) and are always re-checked client-side. Byte arrays support equality only. Columns with a value converter compare their provider values.
Thread safety: not thread-safe while translating; immutable afterwards.

member.summary: Evaluates trees client-side against Cosmos DB documents with the C# semantics of : everything a does not push down (residual predicates, navigations, collection predicates, computed values, ordering, paging and aggregates). Values are compared in their stored form (enum names, converter provider values, JSON text): properties are decoded with and parameter values converted with . member.summary:
A repository stored in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL: the complete surface from over a , except transactions (see ). Repositories created over the same backend (or over backends using the same account and database) share data, so includes and navigation predicates work across entity types. member.name: T:Durable.CosmosDb.CosmosDbRepositorySettings
member.summary:
Settings for a : which account and database to use (an existing , an endpoint and key, a connection string, or the local emulator), how an owned client connects (connection mode, endpoint discovery, timeouts), how storage is provisioned (database and container throughput, creation on first use), how entities are partitioned (), and how the backend behaves (JSON columns, logging, conflict retries).
Account: exactly one of (never disposed by Durable; the client options below then do not apply), with , or . A client built from the endpoint or connection string is owned and disposed by the backend.
Partitioning: by default every entity is partitioned by its document id (/id, one logical partition per document), which spreads load evenly, makes every key lookup a point read and needs no design work, but means every filter that does not name a key is a cross-partition query. Map an entity to one of its properties (for example a tenant or customer id) with to keep related documents together and make queries that filter on that property single-partition; key lookups then need the partition key value (point reads when the property is part of the primary key, otherwise a cross-partition query by id), and Durable checks key uniqueness across partitions with an extra query on insert (Cosmos DB ids are unique only within a partition).
Thread safety: not thread-safe; configure before creating the backend. The backend reads the settings once, when it is created; later changes have no effect on it.
